newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks shake off weakness and end higher.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks shake off weakness and end higher.

text.p: Swiss shares shook off early weakness to close near the day's highs, profiting from gains in some blue chip shares.
"I am very surprised the market held so well, it did not look that way in the beginning", a dealer said, citing Thursday's losses on Wall Street.

The bourse may have overcome its recent consolidation move and may have gathered strength for a rise next week, a trader noted. There is a strong support level around 3,730/35 points in the blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI), he added.
The SMI ended up 0.14 percent, or 5.1 points, to 3,758.7 and the broad SPI up 0.16 percent, or 3.78 points, to 2,413.20.

Strength in blue-chip stocks Roche, Swiss Re and CS Holding gave the market a strong undercurrent from the start, dealers said. U.S. durable goods data first triggered some selling, but the bourse swung back quickly. Volumes were moderate.
Swiss Re continued to shine after Thursday's favourable news from German competitor Muenchner Rueck, jumping almost one percent to 1,354.
"Swiss Re has a tremendous market at the moment", a dealer said, adding the stock appeared to be heading toward new record levels.
Roche and CS Holding put on around 0.2 percent each, while Ciba and Sandoz shares were also up.
Holderbank continued to fall, losing seven francs to 883.
Clariant lost two francs to 445 after Thursday's marked gains.
Sulzer shrugged of early lows after the company said nine-month orders were down two percent and that a lower 1996 group net profit was expected. The shares climbed two francs.
Swissair stocks jumped almost three percent to 991 after Thursday's marked losses.
Computer mouse maker Logitech continued to soar after favourable half-year figures released Thursday.
Bourse newcomer Tag Heuer and Maag both jumped around four percent.
